passages.text: By the sky, which brings back the rain again and again,

passages.title: Chapter 0: Before creation: in the film
passages.text: Whether anything came before the beginning of time lies beyond what physics can test.

passages.title: Chapter 0: Before creation: in the film
passages.text: The Quran speaks of creation coming to be through a single word of command.

passages.title: Chapter 0: Before creation: Open questions
passages.text: Some proposals describe a phase before the hot Big Bang, such as eternal inflation or a bounce from an earlier contracting universe. None has been confirmed by observation.

passages.title: Chapter 0: Before creation: Open questions
passages.text: Did time itself have a beginning, or does the earliest moment we can describe mark only the edge of our present theories?

passages.title: Chapter 0: Before creation: Classical commentators
passages.text: On the command in 2:117 and 36:82, Ibn Kathir explains that it shows the completeness of His power and authority. What He wills comes to be by His command alone, and a single command is enough: it needs no repeating or confirming.

passages.title: Chapter 0: Before creation: Classical commentators
passages.text: On 2:117, Ibn Kathir explains that Allah is called the Originator of the heavens and the earth because He created them when nothing like them had existed before. He quotes al-Tabari’s commentary to the same effect, that they were brought into being without any precedent, and calls that explanation sound.

passages.title: Chapter 0: Before creation: Classical commentators
passages.text: A hadith states the first thing Allah created was the Pen, commanded to write. Many scholars, including Ibn Hajar, understood this to mean first after the Throne and the water, or first in the command to write, since other authentic hadith mention the Throne already over the water.

passages.title: Chapter 0: Before creation: What science measures today
passages.text: Physics has no tested description of what, if anything, came before the beginning of cosmic time. Our best-tested theories trace the history of the universe back about 13.8 billion years, to a hot, dense state.

passages.title: Chapter 0: Before creation: What science measures today
passages.text: Closer still to the first instant, general relativity is expected to break down, and a tested theory of quantum gravity does not yet exist. In general relativity, time is part of the universe being described, not a stage set apart from it.

passages.title: Chapter 1: The beginning: in the film
passages.text: Our universe can be traced back to a beginning that was hot and dense beyond imagining.

passages.title: Chapter 1: The beginning: in the film
passages.text: As space expanded, the young universe cooled.

passages.title: Chapter 1: The beginning: in the film
passages.text: How the beginning itself came to be remains one of the deepest open questions in science.

passages.title: Chapter 1: The beginning: in the film
passages.text: The verse and the science are placed side by side for reflection, not as proof of one another.

passages.title: Chapter 1: The beginning: in the film
passages.text: Space itself stretches, carrying everything within it.

passages.title: Chapter 1: The beginning: Open questions
passages.text: What happened at the very first instant, where today’s physics breaks down?

passages.title: Chapter 1: The beginning: Open questions
passages.text: Did inflation happen, and if so, what drove it? Primordial gravitational waves imprinted on the microwave background would be strong evidence; none has been detected so far.

passages.title: Chapter 1: The beginning: Classical commentators
passages.text: In his commentary on 21:30, Ibn Kathir explains that in the beginning the heavens and the earth were joined together, one upon another. Then Allah (glorified and exalted is He) separated them, made the heavens seven and the earth seven, and placed the air between the earth and the lowest heaven. He cites Sa’id ibn Jubayr, that the earth became separate when the sky was raised, and al-Hasan and Qatadah, that the two were separated by the air between them.

passages.title: Chapter 1: The beginning: Classical commentators
passages.text: Ibn Kathir also records another early report, from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him). The sky was closed and gave no rain, and the earth was closed and grew no plants, until both were opened: the sky with rain and the earth with vegetation.

passages.title: Chapter 1: The beginning: Modern readings
passages.text: Some modern writers read 21:30 as resembling the Big Bang. This is a modern reading, not the classical one.

passages.title: Chapter 1: The beginning: What science measures today
passages.text: The universe is 13.787 billion years old, give or take 20 million years. The figure comes from the Planck satellite’s measurements of the cosmic microwave background, together with the way matter bends that light on its way to us (gravitational lensing) and with maps of how galaxies cluster. It assumes the standard model of cosmology, ΛCDM.

passages.title: Chapter 1: The beginning: What science measures today
passages.text: The Big Bang was not an explosion into empty space. Space itself has been expanding everywhere, carrying distant galaxies apart and stretching their light to longer wavelengths.

passages.title: Chapter 1: The beginning: What science measures today
passages.text: Several separate lines of evidence point to a hot, dense early universe. Space is expanding. The lightest elements exist in the amounts that early heat would make. And the cosmic microwave background, an almost perfect glow of heat, still fills the sky, cooled today to 2.725 kelvin.

passages.title: Chapter 1: The beginning: What science measures today
passages.text: Cosmic inflation proposes a brief burst of extremely rapid expansion in the first instant. It would explain why the universe looks so uniform on large scales and where its first tiny ripples came from. It fits the microwave background well and is well supported, but it has not been directly confirmed.

passages.title: Chapter 2: The first light: in the film
passages.text: As it cooled, electrons joined nuclei to form the first atoms, and the universe became transparent.

passages.title: Chapter 2: The first light: in the film
passages.text: In its first few minutes, the universe forged helium and traces of other light nuclei from protons and neutrons.

passages.title: Chapter 2: The first light: in the film
passages.text: For a long age afterwards, light could not travel freely through the hot, glowing plasma.

passages.title: Chapter 2: The first light: in the film
passages.text: That light still reaches us, stretched into microwaves. This is the real sky map of it from ESA’s Planck satellite.

passages.title: Chapter 2: The first light: in the film
passages.text: Its faint variations in temperature trace the seeds from which galaxies would later grow.

passages.title: Chapter 2: The first light: Open questions
passages.text: The primordial amount of helium-3 is still poorly known: it can be measured only in the Solar System and in gas within our own Galaxy, both long since processed by stars.

passages.title: Chapter 2: The first light: Open questions
passages.text: The cosmological lithium problem. The standard theory of how the first nuclei formed (Big Bang nucleosynthesis) gives 4.72 ± 0.7 lithium-7 atoms for every ten billion hydrogen atoms, about 3.3 times more than old stars show (1.45 ± 0.25). Whether the cause lies in how stars destroy lithium, in nuclear data, or in new physics is not known.

passages.title: Chapter 2: The first light: Classical commentators
passages.text: The commentators also note that in these verses the earth’s creation is mentioned before the heavens were shaped. Ibn Kathir explains that Allah (glorified and exalted is He) created the earth first because it is the foundation, laid before the roof. He reconciles this with 79:30 through a reply of Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him), recorded by al-Bukhari. The earth itself was created first; its spreading out came after the heavens were made.

passages.title: Chapter 2: The first light: Classical commentators
passages.text: Classical commentators describe the smoke (dukhan) in this verse as steam or vapour. Ibn Kathir, commenting on 41:11, explains it as steam that rose up when the earth was created.

passages.title: Chapter 2: The first light: What science measures today
passages.text: In its first few minutes, the universe forged the lightest nuclei. Ordinary matter emerged as about 75.5% hydrogen and 24.5 ± 0.3% helium by mass, or roughly 92% hydrogen and 8% helium by number of atoms.

passages.title: Chapter 2: The first light: What science measures today
passages.text: That light, stretched by the expansion of space, reaches us today as the cosmic microwave background, with a temperature of 2.72548 ± 0.00057 kelvin. The map shows the Planck satellite’s measurement of its tiny temperature differences across the whole sky.

passages.title: Chapter 2: The first light: What science measures today
passages.text: For about 380,000 years the universe was filled with a hot, opaque plasma in which light could not travel far. Once it had cooled to about 3,000 kelvin, electrons and nuclei combined into neutral atoms and light was set free. This last scattering of light happened at a redshift of about 1,090.

passages.title: Chapter 2: The first light: What science measures today
passages.text: Small traces of other light nuclei formed too: 25.08 ± 0.29 deuterium atoms for every million hydrogen atoms, a little helium-3, and a little lithium-7. The oldest stars show 1.45 ± 0.25 lithium-7 atoms for every ten billion hydrogen atoms, though they may have destroyed some of their own lithium.

passages.title: Chapter 3: The dark ages and first stars: in the film
passages.text: After the first light, the universe went dark.

passages.title: Chapter 3: The dark ages and first stars: in the film
passages.text: Around the first stars, the first galaxies began to grow.

passages.title: Chapter 3: The dark ages and first stars: in the film
passages.text: Shown in false colour: dark matter itself gives off no light.

passages.title: Chapter 3: The dark ages and first stars: in the film
passages.text: How the first galaxies formed so quickly remains an open question.

passages.title: Chapter 3: The dark ages and first stars: in the film
passages.text: In its densest knots, the first stars began to shine.

passages.title: Chapter 3: The dark ages and first stars: in the film
passages.text: Unseen matter gathered into a vast web.

passages.title: Chapter 3: The dark ages and first stars: in the film
passages.text: Telescopes today see galaxies from this early age, brighter than many expected.

passages.title: Chapter 3: The dark ages and first stars: Open questions
passages.text: Why are these early galaxies brighter, and why did they appear sooner, than many models expected? It is an open question.

passages.title: Chapter 3: The dark ages and first stars: Open questions
passages.text: No first-generation star has yet been seen directly.

passages.title: Chapter 3: The dark ages and first stars: What science measures today
passages.text: After the first light was set free, no stars yet shone. For millions of years the universe was dark: astronomers call this time the cosmic dark ages.

passages.title: Chapter 3: The dark ages and first stars: What science measures today
passages.text: The first stars probably formed in the densest knots, between about 99 and 178 million years after the beginning (from a redshift of about 30 onward, in current models). They were made almost entirely of hydrogen and helium.

passages.title: Chapter 3: The dark ages and first stars: What science measures today
passages.text: The James Webb Space Telescope has confirmed galaxies shining remarkably early. MoM-z14, at redshift 14.44, is seen as it was about 283 million years after the beginning. JADES-GS-z14-0 was first measured at redshift 14.32 from its JWST spectrum, and ALMA has since pinned it to 14.18: about 290 million years after the beginning.

passages.title: Chapter 3: The dark ages and first stars: What science measures today
passages.text: The web on screen grows by the Zel’dovich approximation, a standard first approximation to how gravity amplifies those first ripples; full simulations follow the collapse further. Dark matter itself is invisible, so it is drawn here in false colour.

passages.title: Chapter 3: The dark ages and first stars: What science measures today
passages.text: Dark matter, which gives off no light but makes up most of the matter in the universe, drew together under its own gravity. The tiny differences in density seen in the cosmic microwave background grew into a vast web of sheets, filaments and knots.

passages.title: Chapter 4: A vast heaven: in the film
passages.text: Across the universe, galaxies gather in countless numbers.

passages.title: Chapter 4: A vast heaven: in the film
passages.text: Light from distant galaxies arrives stretched toward the red.

passages.title: Chapter 4: A vast heaven: in the film
passages.text: The verse and the science are placed side by side for reflection, not as proof of one another.

passages.title: Chapter 4: A vast heaven: in the film
passages.text: Space itself grows, and carries the galaxies apart.

passages.title: Chapter 4: A vast heaven: in the film
passages.text: Two ways of measuring the expansion disagree, and no one yet knows why.

passages.title: Chapter 4: A vast heaven: Open questions
passages.text: What is dark energy, and does it change over time?

passages.title: Chapter 4: A vast heaven: Open questions
passages.text: Is the Hubble tension a sign of unrecognised errors in the measurements, or of new physics?

passages.title: Chapter 4: A vast heaven: Classical commentators
passages.text: Al-Qurtubi records further readings: “We are capable” (Ibn Abbas) and “We are able” (al-Hasan); that Allah widens provision for His creation, through rain (al-Hasan); and “rich and capable”. He concludes that all of these fall within the verse’s meaning.

passages.title: Chapter 4: A vast heaven: Classical commentators
passages.text: Ibn Kathir explains bi-aydin (literally “with hands”) as “with strength”, following Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him), Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Thawri and others. On la-musi‘un he says that Allah (glorified and exalted is He) made the sky vast and raised it high without pillars, so that it stands on its own.

passages.title: Chapter 4: A vast heaven: Modern readings
passages.text: Some modern writers read la-musi‘un as “We are expanding it” and relate it to the expansion of the universe. This is a modern reading, not how the classical commentators explained the verse.

passages.title: Chapter 4: A vast heaven: What science measures today
passages.text: In 1998 two teams studying distant exploding stars found that the expansion is speeding up.

passages.title: Chapter 4: A vast heaven: What science measures today
passages.text: The simplest explanation for the speeding up is a cosmological constant: a dark energy that never changes. But DESI’s 2025 results, combined with the microwave background and supernovae, prefer a dark energy that weakens over time, at 2.8 to 4.2 sigma depending on which supernovae are used. That is a hint, not yet a discovery.

passages.title: Chapter 4: A vast heaven: What science measures today
passages.text: In 1929 Edwin Hubble showed that the farther away a galaxy is, the faster it moves away from us: the universe is expanding.

passages.title: Chapter 4: A vast heaven: What science measures today
passages.text: Galaxies are not flying apart through space; the space between them is growing. Light crossing that growing space is stretched to longer, redder wavelengths. This is its redshift.

passages.title: Chapter 4: A vast heaven: What science measures today
passages.text: Measurements disagree on how fast the universe is expanding today. Inferences from the early universe give 67.4 kilometres per second per megaparsec (Planck) to 68.4 (ACT with Planck and DESI), while nearby stars and supernovae (SH0ES) give 73. This “Hubble tension” is unresolved.

passages.title: Chapter 5: Seven heavens and the galaxies: in the film
passages.text: Our home galaxy, the Milky Way, shown as an artist’s model.

passages.title: Chapter 5: Seven heavens and the galaxies: in the film
passages.text: Everything we can observe lies within the distance light has travelled since the beginning.

passages.title: Chapter 5: Seven heavens and the galaxies: in the film
passages.text: Drawing back, our galaxy becomes one point of light among many.

passages.title: Chapter 5: Seven heavens and the galaxies: in the film
passages.text: Each point of light now is a real galaxy, mapped by the Sloan Digital Sky Survey.

passages.title: Chapter 5: Seven heavens and the galaxies: Open questions
passages.text: Does the universe beyond our horizon look like the part we can see? It cannot be observed, so for now no one can say.

passages.title: Chapter 5: Seven heavens and the galaxies: Open questions
passages.text: Most of the matter shaping this web is dark matter. What it is remains unknown.

passages.title: Chapter 5: Seven heavens and the galaxies: Classical commentators
passages.text: The Quran affirms seven heavens. Most classical scholars understood them as real realms, largely beyond what we can observe.

passages.title: Chapter 5: Seven heavens and the galaxies: Modern readings
passages.text: Some modern writers have tried to match the seven heavens with layers of the atmosphere or with structures in the cosmos. Such matchings are modern and are not made here: this scene shows only observable structure and does not identify the seven heavens with it.

passages.title: Chapter 5: Seven heavens and the galaxies: What science measures today
passages.text: Galaxies grew where gas fell into the knots of the dark-matter web, cooled and formed stars. Ours, the Milky Way, is a barred spiral galaxy. It is shown here as an artist’s model, since we cannot see it from outside.

passages.title: Chapter 5: Seven heavens and the galaxies: What science measures today
passages.text: The observable universe is far larger still. Its radius today is about 46 billion light-years, larger than the light-travel time alone suggests, because space kept expanding while the oldest light was on its way.

passages.title: Chapter 5: Seven heavens and the galaxies: What science measures today
passages.text: Every other point of light here is a real galaxy at its measured position. They are 420,000 galaxies from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey’s twentieth data release, out to redshift 0.8; their light set out up to 7 billion years ago.

passages.title: Chapter 5: Seven heavens and the galaxies: What science measures today
passages.text: Together they trace the cosmic web: walls and filaments of galaxies around vast, emptier voids. The survey’s shape comes from where its telescope could look, mostly away from the dusty plane of our own galaxy. Later the view brightens one slice along the celestial equator, about 160 million light-years thick. The long arc of galaxies across it is the Sloan Great Wall, found in this survey’s maps.

passages.title: Chapter 6: Stars and iron: in the film
passages.text: The core collapses; a shock wave and a flood of neutrinos tear the star apart.

passages.title: Chapter 6: Stars and iron: in the film
passages.text: Its debris carries the elements it made out into space.

passages.title: Chapter 6: Stars and iron: in the film
passages.text: At its heart, fusion reaches iron, and can go no further.

passages.title: Chapter 6: Stars and iron: in the film
passages.text: A massive star burns heavier and heavier elements, layer upon layer.

passages.title: Chapter 6: Stars and iron: in the film
passages.text: It explodes as a Type Ia supernova, forging much of the universe’s iron.

passages.title: Chapter 6: Stars and iron: in the film
passages.text: Much of the iron on Earth, and in our blood, was made in such stars.

passages.title: Chapter 6: Stars and iron: in the film
passages.text: Elsewhere, a white dwarf draws gas from a companion star.

passages.title: Chapter 6: Stars and iron: Open questions
passages.text: Exactly how the shock wave of a core-collapse supernova is revived to blow the star apart is still being worked out.

passages.title: Chapter 6: Stars and iron: Open questions
passages.text: Which kinds of star systems explode as Type Ia supernovae is still debated.

passages.title: Chapter 6: Stars and iron: Classical commentators
passages.text: Al-Qurtubi records that “We sent down” (anzalna) is read by some, among them al-Hasan, as “We brought into being”, just as livestock are said to be “sent down” in 39:6. Ibn Zayd and others read it as Allah (glorified and exalted is He) bringing iron out of the earth and teaching people to work it.

passages.title: Chapter 6: Stars and iron: Classical commentators
passages.text: Ibn Kathir explains the “great might” (ba’s shadid) of iron as weapons of war, a deterrent against those who reject the truth once it has been made clear. Its benefits for people he explains as the tools of daily life: for crafts, for farming and for the home.

passages.title: Chapter 6: Stars and iron: Modern readings
passages.text: Some modern writers read anzalna al-hadid as iron arriving from space, in meteorites or from exploding stars. This is a modern reading, and it is debated.

passages.title: Chapter 6: Stars and iron: What science measures today
passages.text: When the iron core of a massive star can no longer hold itself up, it collapses in a fraction of a second. A shock wave and a burst of neutrinos then blow the star apart in a core-collapse supernova, scattering the elements it made into space.

passages.title: Chapter 6: Stars and iron: What science measures today
passages.text: Silicon burning makes nickel-56, which decays through cobalt-56 into stable iron-56, with half-lives of 6.075 and 77.236 days.

passages.title: Chapter 6: Stars and iron: What science measures today
passages.text: Massive stars fuse ever heavier elements in nested shells: hydrogen, helium, carbon, oxygen and silicon. Fusion stops at the “iron peak”: beyond it, fusing nuclei releases no more energy.

passages.title: Chapter 6: Stars and iron: What science measures today
passages.text: A white dwarf in a close pair of stars can also explode, as a Type Ia supernova. By recent estimates, these thermonuclear explosions made about half of the universe’s iron, and core-collapse supernovae most of the rest.

passages.title: Chapter 6: Stars and iron: What science measures today
passages.text: Much of the iron on Earth, including the iron in our blood, was made in such stars.

passages.title: Chapter 7: The Sun and its course: in the film
passages.text: About 4.6 billion years ago, a cloud of gas and dust collapsed into a spinning disk around a newborn star.

passages.title: Chapter 7: The Sun and its course: in the film
passages.text: The Sun is moving too, carrying the planets around the centre of the Milky Way about once every 230 million years.

passages.title: Chapter 7: The Sun and its course: in the film
passages.text: Within the disk, dust grew into ever larger bodies, and the growing planets swept lanes clear around them.

passages.title: Chapter 7: The Sun and its course: in the film
passages.text: This is the science of the Sun’s motion. It is not presented as the meaning of the verse.

passages.title: Chapter 7: The Sun and its course: in the film
passages.text: These are the planets’ real orbits and positions for today, from NASA JPL data. Sizes and distances are not to scale.

passages.title: Chapter 7: The Sun and its course: in the film
passages.text: The leftover gas was blown away, leaving the planets on their orbits.

passages.title: Chapter 7: The Sun and its course: in the film
passages.text: At the centre the Sun began to shine, fusing hydrogen into helium.

passages.title: Chapter 7: The Sun and its course: Open questions
passages.text: Exactly how dust grains grew into planets is still being worked out.

passages.title: Chapter 7: The Sun and its course: Open questions
passages.text: Many planetary systems found around other stars are arranged very differently from ours. Why is an open question.

passages.title: Chapter 7: The Sun and its course: Classical commentators
passages.text: Ibn Kathir explains “each in an orbit, floating” as revolving, each in its own course. He reports Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) saying that they revolve “like a spinning wheel, in a circle”.

passages.title: Chapter 7: The Sun and its course: Classical commentators
passages.text: Ibn ʿĀshūr, in al-Taḥrīr wa-l-Tanwīr on 21:33, counts kullun fī falakin among the text’s embellishments (badīʿ): its letters read alike from either end, a figure al-Sakkākī named al-maqlūb al-mustawī. It is a literary feature, not a proof of anything.

passages.title: Chapter 7: The Sun and its course: Classical commentators
passages.text: Ibn Kathir records two views of the sun’s “resting place” (li-mustaqarrin laha). In the first, it is beneath the Throne, as in the hadith of Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) recorded by al-Bukhari. In the second, it is the end of the sun’s appointed term on the Day of Resurrection; Qatadah said it has an appointed time that it will not go beyond. He also notes that Ibn Mas’ud and Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them) recited it as “the sun runs with no resting place”: it never stops.

passages.title: Chapter 7: The Sun and its course: Modern readings
passages.text: Some modern writers read 36:38 as describing the Sun’s motion through the galaxy. This is a modern reading. The film shows that motion as science only, not as the meaning of the verse.

passages.title: Chapter 7: The Sun and its course: What science measures today
passages.text: Around the young Sun, gas and dust settled into a flat, spinning disk, and the planets grew within it.

passages.title: Chapter 7: The Sun and its course: What science measures today
passages.text: The Sun and its planets formed from a collapsing cloud of gas and dust about 4.567 billion years ago, the age of the oldest solids found in meteorites.

passages.title: Chapter 7: The Sun and its course: What science measures today
passages.text: The Sun also orbits the centre of the Milky Way, once in roughly 230 million years.

passages.title: Chapter 7: The Sun and its course: What science measures today
passages.text: The planets here move on their real orbits, computed for today’s date from NASA JPL’s orbital elements, and the Moon’s phase is the real one from JPL Horizons. Sizes and distances are compressed so that everything fits: they are not to scale.

passages.title: Chapter 8: The earth spread out: in the film
passages.text: Leftover bodies from the disk still struck it as it grew.

passages.title: Chapter 8: The earth spread out: in the film
passages.text: Over billions of years, the moving plates of the crust raised continents and mountain ranges.

passages.title: Chapter 8: The earth spread out: in the film
passages.text: A giant impact is thought to have thrown out the debris that became the Moon, some 30 to 100 million years after the solar system began; the timing is debated.

passages.title: Chapter 8: The earth spread out: in the film
passages.text: About 4.54 billion years ago the young Earth was a world of molten rock.

passages.title: Chapter 8: The earth spread out: in the film
passages.text: The debris gathered into the Moon.

passages.title: Chapter 8: The earth spread out: in the film
passages.text: As the surface cooled, water rained out of the steam. Tiny zircon crystals show there was liquid water by about 4.4 billion years ago.

passages.title: Chapter 8: The earth spread out: in the film
passages.text: The plates are still moving today.

passages.title: Chapter 8: The earth spread out: Open questions
passages.text: How the Moon-forming impact happened, and exactly when, is still debated.

passages.title: Chapter 8: The earth spread out: Open questions
passages.text: When plate tectonics began on the Earth is not settled.

passages.title: Chapter 8: The earth spread out: Classical commentators
passages.text: Ibn Kathir explains “He spread the earth” (dahaha) by the words that follow it: He brought forth from it its water and its pasture, and set the mountains firm.

passages.title: Chapter 8: The earth spread out: Classical commentators
passages.text: Scholars differed on whether these are ordinary days or longer periods. The Quran also speaks of a Day “whose measure is a thousand years of what you count” (32:5), and of one of fifty thousand years (70:4).

passages.title: Chapter 8: The earth spread out: Classical commentators
passages.text: Ibn Kathir explains that the “four days” of 41:10 include the two days of 41:9: the earth in two days, and its mountains, blessing and provisions in two more, four in all. With the heavens in two days (41:12), the total is six, as in 7:54.

passages.title: Chapter 8: The earth spread out: Classical commentators
passages.text: On the order of creation, Ibn Kathir follows Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him), in a report recorded by al-Bukhari, and the view preferred by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari. The earth was created before the heaven was shaped, and spread out after it. This reconciles 79:30 (“after that He spread the earth”) with 41:9 to 11.

passages.title: Chapter 8: The earth spread out: Modern readings
passages.text: Some modern writers match the six days to stages of cosmic history. Such matchings are modern. The 13.8-billion-year timeline is science’s model, not an interpretation of the days.

passages.title: Chapter 8: The earth spread out: What science measures today
passages.text: The Earth is about 4.54 billion years old, give or take 0.05 billion years, measured from the lead isotopes of ancient rocks and meteorites.

passages.title: Chapter 8: The earth spread out: What science measures today
passages.text: The Moon is thought to have formed from the debris of a giant impact on the young Earth, some 30 to 100 million years after the solar system’s first solids. The timing is debated.

passages.title: Chapter 8: The earth spread out: What science measures today
passages.text: Zircon crystals show that liquid water, and probably oceans, existed by about 4.4 billion years ago.

passages.title: Chapter 8: The earth spread out: What science measures today
passages.text: The Earth’s rigid outer shell is broken into plates that move a few centimetres a year, building mountain ranges where they collide.

passages.title: Chapter 9: Life from water: in the film
passages.text: The story pauses here, before the first humans.

passages.title: Chapter 9: Life from water: in the film
passages.text: Much later, life spread from the water onto the land.

passages.title: Chapter 9: Life from water: in the film
passages.text: A 2024 genetic study places the last common ancestor of all life today at about 4.2 billion years ago.

passages.title: Chapter 9: Life from water: in the film
passages.text: From about 2.4 billion years ago, oxygen made by microbes began to build up in the air. It rose for good about 2.2 billion years ago.

passages.title: Chapter 9: Life from water: in the film
passages.text: The earliest widely accepted traces of life are about 3.5 billion years old. Older claims, up to about 4.1 billion years, are debated.

passages.title: Chapter 9: Life from water: in the film
passages.text: All known life depends on liquid water.

passages.title: Chapter 9: Life from water: Open questions
passages.text: How life began is not known.

passages.title: Chapter 9: Life from water: Open questions
passages.text: Whether life began in the sea, around deep hot springs, in pools on land or elsewhere is debated.

passages.title: Chapter 9: Life from water: Classical commentators
passages.text: On 24:45 he describes the many kinds of creatures, with their forms, colours and ways of moving, all made from one kind of water.

passages.title: Chapter 9: Life from water: Classical commentators
passages.text: Ibn Kathir explains 21:30 by the rain that falls from the sky and the plants it brings from the earth: people see with their own eyes how creation develops, step by step.

passages.title: Chapter 9: Life from water: Modern readings
passages.text: Scholars differ on biological evolution. Many accept it for other life while holding that Adam, peace be upon him, was specially created. This chapter does not take a side.

passages.title: Chapter 9: Life from water: What science measures today
passages.text: The earliest widely accepted traces of life are about 3.5 billion years old. Claims of older life are debated: structures in Greenland about 3.7 billion years old, graphite in Labrador about 3.95 billion years old, and carbon inside a 4.1-billion-year-old zircon crystal.

passages.title: Chapter 9: Life from water: What science measures today
passages.text: Much later, plants and animals spread from the sea onto the land.

passages.title: Chapter 9: Life from water: What science measures today
passages.text: A 2024 genetic study places the last universal common ancestor of all life at about 4.2 billion years ago, give or take about 0.13 billion years.

passages.title: Chapter 9: Life from water: What science measures today
passages.text: Oxygen made by photosynthesising microbes began to build up in the air about 2.43 billion years ago, rising and falling before it rose for good about 2.22 billion years ago.

passages.title: Chapter 9: Life from water: What science measures today
passages.text: Every living cell we know is mostly water, and all known life needs liquid water.

passages.title: Chapter 10: The folding of the heavens: in the film
passages.text: An artistic image of the heavens folding, not a depiction of the Last Day.

passages.title: Chapter 10: The folding of the heavens: in the film
passages.text: If it weakens, as recent DESI results hint, the expansion could slow, and might even reverse into collapse.

passages.title: Chapter 10: The folding of the heavens: in the film
passages.text: If it grows stronger, it could one day tear apart galaxies, stars and planets.

passages.title: Chapter 10: The folding of the heavens: in the film
passages.text: What comes next depends on dark energy, which is not yet understood. Science offers possibilities, not certainties.

passages.title: Chapter 10: The folding of the heavens: in the film
passages.text: If dark energy stays constant, galaxies drift ever farther apart and the stars burn out: a cold, dark universe.

passages.title: Chapter 10: The folding of the heavens: in the film
passages.text: Today the universe is still expanding, and the expansion is speeding up.

passages.title: Chapter 10: The folding of the heavens: Open questions
passages.text: What dark energy is, and whether it is changing, is unknown.

passages.title: Chapter 10: The folding of the heavens: Open questions
passages.text: Whether the universe will end, and how, cannot be settled by today’s measurements.

passages.title: Chapter 10: The folding of the heavens: Classical commentators
passages.text: On 14:48, he explains that the earth will be changed into an earth other than the one we know.

passages.title: Chapter 10: The folding of the heavens: Classical commentators
passages.text: Ibn Kathir explains 21:104 as the heaven rolled up like a written scroll on the Day of Resurrection. “As We began the first creation, We shall repeat it” he explains as Allah creating His creation anew: as He created them in the first place, He is able to create them again.

passages.title: Chapter 10: The folding of the heavens: Classical commentators
passages.text: On 81:1, Ibn Kathir reports Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) saying the sun will be darkened: it will be folded up and its light will go. On 81:2, the stars will be scattered.

passages.title: Chapter 10: The folding of the heavens: Modern readings
passages.text: Some modern writers compare these verses with scientific ideas about the end of the universe, such as a Big Crunch. These are modern comparisons. Science’s futures are hypotheses about matter; the verses speak of the Day of Resurrection, which lies in the unseen.

passages.title: Chapter 10: The folding of the heavens: What science measures today
passages.text: Since 1998, measurements of distant supernovae have shown that the expansion of the universe is speeding up. The cause is called dark energy.

passages.title: Chapter 10: The folding of the heavens: What science measures today
passages.text: Recent DESI results, combined with other data, hint at 2.8 to 4.2 sigma that dark energy may be weakening. It is not yet a discovery.

passages.title: Chapter 10: The folding of the heavens: What science measures today
passages.text: If dark energy stays constant, the universe expands forever, galaxies drift beyond sight and the stars burn out (a “heat death”). If it grows stronger, it could tear apart galaxies, stars and planets in a “Big Rip”. If it weakens, the expansion could slow and might reverse into a “Big Crunch”.

passages.title: Words to know
passages.text: Al-‘Arsh: the Throne. The hadith in this chapter say it was over the water before the heavens and the earth were created. It is of the unseen and is never pictured.

passages.title: Words to know
passages.text: Badi‘: the Originator, who brings something into being with nothing like it before it (Quran 2:117).

passages.title: Words to know
passages.text: Al-Ghayb: the unseen, what lies beyond our senses and our instruments. The film leaves it unpictured.

passages.title: Words to know
passages.text: Kun, fayakun: “Be!”, and it is. The word of command in Quran 2:117 and 36:82: when Allah (glorified and exalted is He) decrees a thing, He says to it only “Be!”, and it is.

passages.title: Words to know
passages.text: Al-Qalam: the Pen. A hadith says it was the first thing created and was commanded to write; scholars such as Ibn Hajar understood this as first after the Throne and the water.

passages.title: Quran 14:48
passages.text: On the day when the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens (also will be changed) and they will come forth unto Allah, the One, the Almighty,

passages.title: Quran 21:104
passages.text: The Day when We shall roll up the heavens as a recorder rolleth up a written scroll. As We began the first creation, We shall repeat it. (It is) a promise (binding) upon Us. Lo! We are to perform it.

passages.title: Quran 21:30
passages.text: Have not those who disbelieve known that the heavens and the earth were of one piece, then We parted them, and we made every living thing of water? Will they not then believe?

passages.title: Quran 21:33
passages.text: And He it is Who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon. They float, each in an orbit.

passages.title: Quran 22:47
passages.text: And they will bid thee hasten on the Doom, and Allah faileth not His promise, but lo! a Day with Allah is as a thousand years of what ye reckon.

passages.title: Quran 24:45
passages.text: Allah hath created every animal of water. Of them is (a kind) that goeth upon its belly and (a kind) that goeth upon two legs and (a kind) that goeth upon four. Allah createth what He will. Lo! Allah is Able to do all things.

passages.title: Quran 25:59
passages.text: Who created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six Days, then He mounted the Throne. The Beneficent! Ask anyone informed concerning Him!

passages.title: Quran 2:117
passages.text: The Originator of the heavens and the earth! When He decreeth a thing, He saith unto it only: Be! and it is.

passages.title: Quran 32:4
passages.text: Allah it is Who created the heavens and the earth, and that which is between them, in six Days. Then He mounted the Throne. Ye have not, beside Him, a protecting friend or mediator. Will ye not then remember?

passages.title: Quran 32:5
passages.text: He directeth the ordinance from the heaven unto the earth; then it ascendeth unto Him in a Day, whereof the measure is a thousand years of that ye reckon.

passages.title: Quran 36:38
passages.text: And the sun runneth on unto a resting-place for him. That is the measuring of the Mighty, the Wise.

passages.title: Quran 36:39
passages.text: And for the moon We have appointed mansions till she return like an old shrivelled palm-leaf.

passages.title: Quran 36:40
passages.text: It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor doth the night outstrip the day. They float each in an orbit.

passages.title: Quran 36:82
passages.text: But His command, when He intendeth a thing, is only that He saith unto it: Be! and it is.

passages.title: Quran 39:6
passages.text: He created you from one being, then from that (being) He made its mate; and He hath provided for you of cattle eight kinds. He created you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, in a threefold gloom. Such is Allah, your Lord. His is the Sovereignty. There is no Allah save Him. How then are ye turned away?

passages.title: Quran 39:67
passages.text: And they esteem not Allah as He hath the right to be esteemed, when the whole earth is His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens are rolled in His right hand. Glorified is He and High Exalted from all that they ascribe as partner (unto Him).

passages.title: Quran 41:10
passages.text: He placed therein firm hills rising above it, and blessed it and measured therein its sustenance in four Days, alike for (all) who ask;

passages.title: Quran 41:11
passages.text: Then turned He to the heaven when it was smoke, and said unto it and unto the earth: Come both of you, willingly or loth. They said: We come, obedient.

passages.title: Quran 41:12
passages.text: Then He ordained them seven heavens in two Days and inspired in each heaven its mandate; and We decked the nether heaven with lamps, and rendered it inviolable. That is the measuring of the Mighty, the Knower.

passages.title: Quran 41:9
passages.text: Say (O Muhammad, unto the idolaters): Disbelieve ye verily in Him Who created the earth in two Days, and ascribe ye unto Him rivals? He (and none else) is the Lord of the Worlds.

passages.title: Quran 50:38
passages.text: And verily We created the heavens and the earth, and all that is between them, in six Days, and naught of weariness touched Us.

passages.title: Quran 51:47
passages.text: We have built the heaven with might, and We it is Who make the vast extent (thereof).

passages.title: Quran 55:33
passages.text: O company of jinn and men, if ye have power to penetrate (all) regions of the heavens and the earth, then penetrate (them)! Ye will never penetrate them save with (Our) sanction.

passages.title: Quran 57:25
passages.text: We verily sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and revealed with them the Scripture and the Balance, that mankind may observe right measure; and He revealed iron, wherein is mighty power and (many) uses for mankind, and that Allah may know him who helpeth Him and His messengers, though unseen. Lo! Allah is Strong, Almighty.

passages.title: Quran 65:12
passages.text: Allah it is who hath created seven heavens, and of the earth the like thereof. The commandment cometh down among them slowly, that ye may know that Allah is Able to do all things, and that Allah surroundeth all things in knowledge.

passages.title: Quran 67:3
passages.text: Who hath created seven heavens in harmony. Thou (Muhammad) canst see no fault in the Beneficent One's creation; then look again: Canst thou see any rifts?

passages.title: Quran 70:4
passages.text: (Whereby) the angels and the Spirit ascend unto Him in a Day whereof the span is fifty thousand years.

passages.title: Quran 79:30
passages.text: And after that He spread the earth,

passages.title: Quran 79:31
passages.text: And produced therefrom the water thereof and the pasture thereof,

passages.title: Quran 79:32
passages.text: And He made fast the hills,

passages.title: Quran 7:54
passages.text: Lo! your Lord is Allah Who created the heavens and the earth in six Days, then mounted He the Throne. He covereth the night with the day, which is in haste to follow it, and hath made the sun and the moon and the stars subservient by His command. His verily is all creation and commandment. Blessed be Allah, the Lord of the Worlds!

passages.title: Quran 81:1
passages.text: When the sun is overthrown,

passages.title: Quran 81:2
passages.text: And when the stars fall,

passages.title: Quran 82:1
passages.text: When the heaven is cleft asunder,

passages.title: Quran 82:2
passages.text: When the planets are dispersed,

passages.title: Quran 86:11
passages.text: By the heaven which giveth the returning rain,
